## Chapter Map {#chapter-map .section-title}

```{=html}
<div class="wh-book-grid wh-reveal">
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 1</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./why-scientific-computing-matters.html">Why Scientific Computing Matters</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">What becomes possible once you have the machinery set up, and why geographers need code rather than just GUI tools. No setup required.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 2</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./your-first-python-script.html">Your First Python Script</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Write and run Python in your browser right now — no installation. Print text, do math, write a conditional. Code is just instructions you write.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 3</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./command-line-essentials.html">Command Line Essentials</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Navigate your computer without a mouse. Learn <code>pwd</code>, <code>ls</code>, <code>cd</code>, and <code>mkdir</code> — the four commands Python needs you to know first.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 4</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./installing-python.html">Installing Python</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Anaconda vs standard Python — which path fits your work. Step-by-step instructions for Windows, Mac, and Linux. Verify it works before moving on.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 5</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./virtual-environments.html">Virtual Environments</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Why global installations cause dependency conflicts. Create, activate, and deactivate isolated sandboxes using <code>venv</code> or <code>conda</code>.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 6</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./package-management.html">Installing Packages</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Expand Python with <code>pip</code> and <code>conda</code>. Install NumPy, SciPy, and geographic libraries. Freeze your setup into <code>requirements.txt</code> for reproducibility.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 7</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./your-first-jupyter-notebook.html">Jupyter Notebooks</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Install and launch Jupyter, write code and markdown cells, run them in sequence. The interactive environment you'll use throughout all three pathways.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 8</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./running-and-debugging-code.html">Running and Debugging</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">The three ways Python runs: shell, notebook, and script. How to read a traceback from the bottom up and fix the five most common error types.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 9</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./ides-and-editors.html">IDEs and Code Editors</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">When to graduate from notebooks to scripts. VSCode vs PyCharm — what each is for and how to point it at your virtual environment.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 10</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./git-and-version-control.html">Git and Version Control</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Track every change to your code. Clone, status, add, commit, push — the five-step lifecycle that replaces <code>model_final_v3_USE_THIS_ONE.py</code>.</div>
  </article>
</div>
```
